title: Lower a lab scissor jack to clear a submerged pH probe, swap the sample beaker for the rinse beaker, and raise it
instruction: Lower the lab scissor jack until the sample beaker clears the fixed pH probe, move the sample beaker onto the blue mat, set the rinse beaker on the jack, and raise the jack until the probe tip sits inside the green immersion band without touching the beaker floor.
context: Wet-lab research technicians clamp combination pH and conductivity electrodes at a fixed height on a support stand and raise or lower vessels beneath them on a DIN 12897 scissor jack so the electrode bulb is never unclamped or struck against a beaker rim (Other: laboratory research automation). The central difficulty is the constrained physical order under a fixed overhead probe, not wheel turning alone: at reset the pH probe extends 16 mm down inside the sample beaker on the raised jack, so pulling the beaker sideways before lowering drives its wall into the submerged shaft, while cranking the rinse beaker too high drives its floor into the probe tip. Both 50 mL polypropylene beakers are dry so no open liquid sits near the shared robot; a 20 to 40 mm green band on the rinse beaker and probe shaft stands in for submerging the sensing bulb and junction into a 40 mL deionized-water rinse.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the bench (fixed layout, object_jitter = 0). Centred at (25.0, +1.5), a BOCHEM Type 1 stainless lab scissor jack (Art. 11120, DIN 12897, 1.65 kg, plates 13.0 cm along x by 16.0 cm along the y scissor axis, height range 6.0 to 27.5 cm) sits on four rubber feet inside pencil corner marks (within 2 mm and 2 degrees), its deck set to z = 8.6 cm with a steel ruler and its 4.0 cm black adjusting wheel on the -y end at y = -11.6 cm, z = 4.3 cm. Behind the jack at (36.5, +1.5), a clamped stainless retort stand holds a Hanna Instruments HI1230B PEI-body combination pH electrode (DIN 19262, 1.2 cm shaft, 16.35 cm overall length, routed to a benchtop meter block at (38.5, +9.0)) vertically coaxial over (25.0, +1.5) with its tip fixed at z = 13.0 cm (within 1 mm). Two dry Thermo Scientific Nalgene 50 mL Griffin low-form polypropylene beakers (Cat. 1201-0050PK, ISO/DIN 7056, 4.8 cm OD x 6.0 cm tall, 2 mm wall and floor; no open liquid on the shared rig): the sample beaker (blue base stripe) starts centred on the jack deck (rim at 14.6 cm, submerging the probe tip 1.6 cm); the rinse beaker (green immersion band 2.0 to 4.0 cm below its rim, standing in for a 40 mL rinse) starts on a 9.0 x 9.0 x 0.3 cm grey silicone pad at (34.0, -19.5) (within 2 mm). A 12.0 x 12.0 x 0.3 cm blue silicone sample mat is fixed at (36.5, +20.5). On a real bench, a level side camera with a millimetre scale behind (25.0, +1.5) records probe deflection and tip-to-floor clearance.
scoring: 0 for good if at any step in the trial video (a) a beaker wall or hand strikes and deflects the pH probe tip laterally more than 4 mm from its rest axis, (b) a beaker's inner floor touches the probe tip (0 mm tip-to-floor gap on the side video), (c) either beaker tilts more than 25 degrees or touches the bare bench outside its silicone pad, or (d) the lab jack base slides more than 25 mm from its bench marks. Otherwise scored at the end once every part of both hands is at least 30 mm clear of the jack, both beakers, and the probe and the deck and both beakers move 2 mm at most over 1.0 s (20 steps). 0.25: the jack deck lowered below 70 mm so the 60 mm sample beaker cleared the 130 mm probe tip, and the sample beaker rests upright (8 degrees tilt at most) wholly inside the 120 x 120 mm blue mat (centre within 36 mm along x and y). 0.5: 0.25 met, and the rinse beaker rests upright (8 degrees at most) on the jack deck coaxial around the probe (horizontal offset 12 mm at most, at least 4 mm clear of the inner wall), with the probe tip outside the 20 to 40 mm band below its rim. 1.0: 0.5 met, and the probe tip sits 20 to 40 mm below the rinse beaker's top rim (deck height 90 to 110 mm, at least 18 mm clear above the beaker floor). 0.0: otherwise. Read on the bench with a steel millimetre ruler, phone inclinometer, side video against the millimetre scale, and end photos.
reset_notes: About 45 seconds between trials: turn the adjusting wheel counterclockwise until the rinse beaker clears the 130 mm probe tip, return the dry rinse beaker to its grey start pad at (34.0, -19.5) cm (within 2 mm), set the jack deck top to 86.0 mm above the bench with a steel ruler (within 1 mm), place the dry sample beaker on the deck centre ring around the probe (within 2 mm), check the jack base sits on its pencil corner marks at (25.0, +1.5) cm (within 2 mm, 2 degrees), and verify the HI1230B tip height is 130.0 mm (within 1 mm). Both polypropylene beakers are durable dry labware; no consumables are used.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies, zero welds. Scissor jack: prismatic deck and half-height carrier coupled two-way to the -y handwheel at 18 mm/rev (capped at 68.7 N), feeding axial deck load back onto the wheel (-F*lead/rad) plus 0.10 N m self-locking thread drag, equal and opposite on the carrier. Dry 16-stave hollow beakers (65 g vs 15 g true for stable 20 N pinch); no liquid is simulated (20-40 mm green band stands in for 40 mL rinse). Witness springs (8.5 N m/rad, 2.5 kN/m; 1.2 mm/3 N floor touch).
